definition: To make brief contact with someone to check on progress or share updates.
business_context_example: Let's touch base on Friday to see where we are with the client proposal.
translation_bg: да се чуем накратко (за докъде сме)

definition: To return to a topic or task later, after dealing with other things first.
business_context_example: I don't have the numbers yet, so let's circle back to the budget after lunch.
translation_bg: да се върнем на темата по-късно

definition: To share the same understanding or agreement about something.
business_context_example: Before we email the vendor, I want to make sure we're on the same page about pricing.
translation_bg: с еднакво разбиране, на едно мнение

definition: To check on something again after a first contact, message, or meeting.
business_context_example: I sent the invoice last week, but I'll follow up today since they haven't replied.
translation_bg: да проследя, да напомня след първия контакт

definition: To show or explain an idea to someone to get their opinion or approval.
business_context_example: Can I run this draft by you before I send it to the whole team?
translation_bg: да покажа нещо на някого за мнение

definition: Informed and included in updates about a project or decision.
business_context_example: Please keep me in the loop about any changes to the delivery schedule.

definition: To stop working, usually because you've done enough for now.
business_context_example: We've fixed the main bug and it's already 7 pm, so let's call it a day.

definition: To take responsibility for a task or project and guide others.
business_context_example: Maria will take the lead on the onboarding project since she knows the client best.

definition: To reply to someone later with an answer or information.
business_context_example: I need to check with my manager first, but I'll get back to you by Thursday.

definition: To make a noticeable difference or real progress on something important.
business_context_example: The new ads brought 3 sales, but honestly that doesn't move the needle for us.

definition: To contact someone, usually to ask for help or start a conversation.
business_context_example: A client from Germany reached out yesterday asking about our group rates.

definition: A short warning or notice that something is going to happen.
business_context_example: Just a heads up: the office internet will be down tomorrow from 9 to 11.

definition: Continue to give me updates as things change.
business_context_example: I can't join the call, so keep me posted on what the client decides.

definition: To start a project, meeting, or event.
business_context_example: We'll kick off the new campaign with a short team meeting on Monday.

definition: To finish or end something, like a meeting or a task.
business_context_example: Let's wrap up this call, we've covered everything on the agenda.

definition: To review or examine something carefully.
business_context_example: Can we go over the contract together before I sign it?

definition: To start talking about a topic in a conversation or meeting.
business_context_example: I didn't want to bring up the salary question in front of everyone.

definition: To mention a topic briefly without discussing it in detail.
business_context_example: The presentation touched on remote work, but the focus was hiring.

definition: To join a conversation by adding a comment or opinion.
business_context_example: Feel free to chime in if you have questions during the demo.

definition: To give your opinion on something being discussed.
business_context_example: Before we choose the logo, I'd like the design team to weigh in.

definition: To say what you think openly, or to talk louder.
business_context_example: If you disagree with the plan, please speak up now, not after we start.
translation_bg: да кажа мнението си на глас

definition: To discuss something privately later, outside the current meeting.
business_context_example: This is getting too detailed for the group, let's take it offline.
translation_bg: да го обсъдим отделно след срещата

definition: Specific tasks that people agree to do after a meeting.
business_context_example: I'll send the action items by email: two for me, one for Ivan.

definition: The main points or lessons you remember from a meeting or event.
business_context_example: My main takeaway from the conference was that clients want shorter courses.

definition: To think of many ideas quickly, usually in a group, without judging them yet.
business_context_example: Let's brainstorm names for the new course before we pick one.

definition: To share ideas with someone to hear their reaction.
business_context_example: Do you have 10 minutes? I want to bounce a few ideas off you.
translation_bg: да обсъдя идеи с някого, за да чуя реакция

definition: To stop small talk and start discussing the important topic.
business_context_example: Coffee's ready, so let's get down to business: the Q3 numbers.

definition: To say or do something that makes people feel relaxed at the start.
business_context_example: He told a short story about his dog to break the ice with the new client.

definition: Light, friendly conversation about unimportant topics.
business_context_example: We made small talk about the weather before the interview started.

definition: To skip the introduction and talk about the main point directly.
business_context_example: I'll cut to the chase: we need the delivery 2 weeks earlier.

definition: A way to give only the short version of a longer story.
business_context_example: Long story short, the supplier canceled and we found a better one.

definition: Said very briefly, using only the main facts.
business_context_example: In a nutshell, the project is late but under budget.

definition: The most important point, or the final financial result.
business_context_example: The bottom line is simple: if we don't sign by Friday, we lose the deal.

definition: The overall situation, not the small details.
business_context_example: Forget the font size for now, let's look at the big picture of the website.

definition: Undecided between two options.
business_context_example: I'm still on the fence about hiring a second designer this year.

definition: To agree with someone about something.
business_context_example: We don't see eye to eye on pricing, but we agree on everything else.

definition: To decide what to do as the situation develops, without a fixed plan.
business_context_example: We don't know how many people will come, so let's play it by ear.

phrase: off the top of my head
definition: Said from memory, without checking or preparing.
business_context_example: Off the top of my head, we have about 40 active students right now.
audio_text: off the top of my head

definition: A big, obvious problem that everyone avoids talking about.
business_context_example: Let's talk about the elephant in the room: our biggest client is leaving.
translation_bg: очевидният проблем, за който никой не говори

definition: To include someone in a conversation or email thread so they stay informed.
business_context_example: Can you loop in the accountant? She needs to see these invoices too.

definition: To send someone a copy of an email so they can follow the conversation.
business_context_example: Please cc me when you reply to the client so I know what was agreed.

definition: To answer an email so that everyone in the thread sees your reply.
business_context_example: Careful with reply all, 30 people don't need to see your lunch plans.

definition: A small mistake in typing, like a wrong or missing letter.
business_context_example: There's a typo in the subject line: it says 'meating' instead of 'meeting'.

definition: To read a text carefully to find and fix mistakes before sending it.
business_context_example: Always proofread the newsletter twice before it goes to 500 people.

definition: To check something a second time to be sure it's correct.
business_context_example: Can you double-check the flight times before I book the hotel?

definition: To officially approve something.
business_context_example: The CFO needs to sign off on any purchase over 1,000 euro.

definition: To finish what you promised or started.
business_context_example: He has great ideas, but he rarely follows through on them.

definition: To find the answer or solution to something after thinking about it.
business_context_example: I can't figure out why the printer works for everyone except me.
translation_bg: да разбера как, да измисля решение

definition: To solve a problem or organize something that was messy.
business_context_example: Give me an hour to sort out the schedule conflict with the two classes.

definition: To handle a problem, task, or person.
business_context_example: I'll deal with the complaint this afternoon, right after my calls.

definition: To delay something until later.
business_context_example: We've put off the website update twice already, let's just do it.

definition: To pause something for a period of time.
business_context_example: The expansion is on hold until we see the summer results.

definition: To remove small problems or disagreements from a plan.
business_context_example: The contract is almost ready, we just need to iron out the payment terms.

definition: To make something exact and final, like a date or a price.
business_context_example: Before Friday we need to nail down the exact start date of the course.

definition: To plan something for a date that may still change.
business_context_example: Let's pencil in Tuesday at 3, and I'll confirm by tomorrow.

definition: To arrange or organize something, like a meeting or a system.
business_context_example: I'll set up a call with the new supplier for Thursday morning.

definition: To cancel something that was planned.
business_context_example: They called off the training because only 2 people signed up.

definition: To create something by combining parts, like a report or a team.
business_context_example: Can you put together a short offer for the hotel chain by Monday?

definition: To think of an idea, plan, or solution.
business_context_example: She came up with a smart way to cut our delivery costs by 15%.

definition: To accept new work or responsibility.
business_context_example: I can't take on another project this month, my schedule is full.

definition: To take control of something from someone else.
business_context_example: When Petar retires in May, his daughter will take over the company.

definition: To do someone's job temporarily while they are away.
business_context_example: Elena will fill in for me while I'm on vacation next week.

definition: To complete a form by writing information in it.
business_context_example: New clients need to fill out this short form before the first lesson.

definition: To give responsibility or an object to someone else.
business_context_example: Before you leave, please hand over the project files to Stefan.
translation_bg: да предам отговорност или нещо на друг

definition: The amount of work I currently have to do.
business_context_example: I'd love to help, but I have too much on my plate this week.

definition: To have enough time and energy for extra work.
business_context_example: Do you have the bandwidth to review 2 more applications today?

definition: To manage several tasks or responsibilities at the same time.
business_context_example: She's juggling 3 client projects and a new hire's training.

definition: To follow and record information so you don't lose or forget it.
business_context_example: We use a simple spreadsheet to keep track of student payments.

definition: To have no time left to finish something.
business_context_example: We ran out of time in the demo, so questions moved to email.

definition: Late compared to the planned schedule.
business_context_example: Sorry, I'm running behind today, can we move our call to 4 pm?

definition: To find time in your schedule for something important.
business_context_example: Even in busy weeks, I make time for a 30-minute review every Friday.

definition: Needing a lot of time to do.
business_context_example: Writing reports by hand is time-consuming, let's use a template.

definition: To lose focus because something else takes your attention.
business_context_example: I got sidetracked by emails and forgot to send the invoice.

definition: With very little warning or time to prepare.
business_context_example: Thanks for joining the call on such short notice.

definition: At the latest possible time, just before a deadline.
business_context_example: The client changed the order at the last minute, again.

definition: Continuing until the very last moment before a deadline.
business_context_example: The proposal went down to the wire, we sent it at 11:58 pm.

definition: A short, stressful period when a lot of work must be finished.
business_context_example: It's crunch time: the launch is Monday and the site isn't ready.

definition: Later than planned.
business_context_example: The renovation is 2 weeks behind schedule because of the permits.

definition: Making progress as planned.
business_context_example: Sales are on track to reach the yearly goal by November.

definition: Not yet decided or certain.
business_context_example: The date for the team retreat is still up in the air.

definition: Being prepared or developed, but not ready yet.
business_context_example: We have 3 new courses in the pipeline for the autumn season.

definition: Starting again from the beginning because the plan failed.
business_context_example: The client rejected all 3 designs, so it's back to the drawing board.

definition: To start a process or activity.
business_context_example: I'll get the ball rolling by booking the venue today.

phrase: the ball is in your court
definition: It's your turn to act or decide.
business_context_example: We sent our best offer yesterday, so the ball is in their court now.
audio_text: the ball is in your court

definition: A small improvement that is easy to achieve and shows fast results.
business_context_example: Fixing the contact form is a quick win, it takes an hour and helps sales.

definition: The easiest tasks or opportunities to start with.
business_context_example: Let's go for the low-hanging fruit first: emailing our old clients.

definition: A decision so easy and obvious that it needs no thought.
business_context_example: The software costs 10 euro and saves us 5 hours a week. It's a no-brainer.

definition: A strategy or plan for achieving a goal.
business_context_example: What's our game plan if the landlord raises the rent?

definition: An alternative plan in case the first one fails.
business_context_example: If the trainer cancels, plan B is to run the workshop online.

definition: A temporary way to solve a problem without fixing its cause.
business_context_example: The payment button is broken, but the workaround is a direct bank link.

definition: Trying different ways and learning from mistakes until something works.
business_context_example: We found the best ad format through trial and error over 3 months.

definition: A simple, practical rule that works in most situations.
business_context_example: As a rule of thumb, we reply to every client email within 24 hours.

definition: To do something cheaply or quickly by skipping important steps.
business_context_example: Don't cut corners on the contract, have a lawyer read it.
translation_bg: да претупам, да спестя важни стъпки

definition: To make a mistake by forgetting or failing to do something.
business_context_example: I dropped the ball on the renewal email and we lost the client.
translation_bg: да изпусна задача, да се издъня

definition: To take responsibility or make a bigger effort when it's needed.
business_context_example: When the manager got sick, Diana stepped up and ran the whole event.
translation_bg: да поема отговорност в труден момент

definition: To do more than what is expected.
business_context_example: She went the extra mile and translated the menu for free.

definition: To do your fair share of the work in a team.
business_context_example: Everyone pulled their weight during the move, so we finished in a day.
translation_bg: да върша своя дял от работата

definition: Someone who works well with others and helps the group succeed.
business_context_example: We're looking for a team player, not a lone star.

definition: To learn how to do a new job or task.
business_context_example: Give the new assistant a month to learn the ropes.

definition: To learn the latest information so you can work effectively.
business_context_example: Read these 2 documents to get up to speed on the project.
